reviewers.summary: The backend, mutation, coverage, and native-lane requirements are substantially aligned with the plan. Delivery is not ready: the artifacts simultaneously claim ordinary queue authorization and state that a fresh governance exception is pending, while the proposed PR-head review does not satisfy the existing final-SHA review contract without that exception. The baseline queue task is also not explicitly dependent on resolving this decision.

The CI-only boundary, data ownership, rollback, mutation aggregation, and native-lane direction are broadly coherent. Two execution contracts still require correction: backend shards would inherit the existing 95% per-invocation coverage gate, and dependent aggregators lack an explicit always-run failure-evidence path. Separately, ordinary merge-queue delivery of the ASK-class baseline and implementation changes requires a fresh, bounded owner permission.

The evidence strategy is broadly proportionate: helper and validator tests cover completeness and fail-closed behavior, while exact-SHA CI, artifacts, protection snapshots, and comparable queue runs cover operational acceptance. Approval is blocked by contradictory landing authorization and by tasks that still combine several independently verifiable outcomes into one non-executable integration lane.

No privacy, consent, or security planning gaps remain. The feature is CI-only and introduces no user-content processing, product authorization path, account record, consent flow, or destructive product action. CI evidence has explicit 7-day PR and 30-day non-PR retention, is excluded from account export/purge because it contains no account data, and is constrained to synthetic identifiers and source-derived results. Raw JUnit remains runner-local; coverage paths must be repository-relative; workspace, home, temporary, absolute, parent-traversal, and unexpected paths fail closed without being echoed. Existing read-only workflow permissions, secret isolation, required-job propagation, and exact-SHA checks are preserved. Consent gating, per-owner scoping, and 404-versus-403 behavior are therefore not applicable rather than omitted.

This lens does not apply. The feature is limited to CI execution and evidence aggregation; design.md explicitly declares no rendered product UI, copy, navigation, accessibility interaction, or mobile journey changes, while plan.md excludes all product code. Per the rubric’s scope guard, loading, empty, error, partial-failure UI, keyboard/focus, mobile viewport, and interruption/resume requirements are therefore not applicable.

The sharding design is generally fail-closed and introduces no product-data migration, public API, consent, or irreversible product-state change. Approval is blocked because this ASK-class change proposes an ordinary merge-queue exception to binding landing and exact-SHA controls, and that exception is explicitly still awaiting the owner’s decision. Current high-risk approval evidence must also be rebound to the corrected artifacts before implementation.

technical_findings.description: The backend-shard execution contract contradicts the repository's current pytest configuration. The plan says each shard runs pytest but does not evaluate the whole-suite floor, while every pytest invocation currently inherits --cov-fail-under=95. Only collection explicitly disables default addopts, and the later statement that existing CLI thresholds remain intact leaves no defined override for partial executions. An implementation following the plan would evaluate each partial shard against the whole-suite threshold before coverage can be combined, violating FR-002's aggregation-before-floor contract.

technical_findings.recommendation: State explicitly that every nonempty shard disables only the per-invocation floor, for example with --cov-fail-under=0 or an equivalent addopts override, while retaining branch/context collection and Allure output. Enforce the unchanged 95% floor only after backend-results combines both databases and produces the canonical XML. Add a workflow-validator assertion that rejects reintroduction of a per-shard floor.

technical_findings.description: The plan makes backend-results and the mutation judge depend on matrix jobs but does not specify always-run job semantics when a dependency fails or is cancelled. Under the current graph pattern, such a dependent job is skipped unless explicitly guarded. Moving canonical backend artifacts and the blocking mutation Allure producer into those jobs can therefore remove diagnostic evidence precisely when a shard fails, despite the accepted fail-closed and retained-diagnostics requirements.

github workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml:1486-1490 shows the current mutation judge depends on both measurements without an always-run job condition, while .github/workflows/ci.yml:1934-1952 demonstrates the repository's explicit if: always() pattern for a failure-reporting dependent job.
technical_findings.recommendation: Define backend-results and the mutation judge as always-running dependent jobs. Their shard upload steps must also run on failure; aggregators should download whatever evidence exists, publish or synthesize diagnostics first, then fail on missing, corrupt, failed, or cancelled inputs. Intentional empty partitions remain acceptable only after their manifests validate. Extend the workflow validator with negative cases that remove the always-run condition or diagnostic upload.
